# Jurgen Halili — Portfolio (full content)

> Solo full-stack engineer with AI focus, based in Kiel, Germany. This file contains the full prose of every case study on this portfolio for AI search engines that prefer single-fetch ingestion over crawling.

## Projects

### Counting a Protest

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/counting-a-protest
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: P2PNet + VisDrone/COCO, OpenCV + FFmpeg, 4K night drone.

Independent crowd count of the 10 June Tirana march — ≈22,000 from one night drone.

Independent measurement of the 10 June 2026 protest in Tirana: ≈22,000 protesters [19,000–25,000] from 29 minutes of stationary 4K night drone footage. Full-width counting strips paced by the crowd's measured turnover, hand-measured detection factors per era of the footage, and five independent instruments converging on the same corridor.

Counting a Protest is the one project here whose deliverable is a single number: ≈22,000 people [19,000–25,000] walked down Bulevardi Dëshmorët e Kombit in Tirana on 10 June 2026, measured from 29 minutes of stationary 4K night drone footage. In Albania crowd numbers are a genre of fiction — organizers and government routinely disagree by 5× — so I built a measurement where every component has a photograph behind it. The architecture is 11 full-width turnover freezes spaced by the crowd's hand-measured 3.6-minute turnover, counted by a VisDrone+COCO detector union plus P2PNet perspective-strip dot fields, with hand-measured per-era detection factors (S3 ×3.75, S4 ×10.3, S5 ×5.27) paying the detection tax — each factor derived by marking entire strips head by head. The decomposition: 20,202 counted inside the 11 freezes, 611 between-freeze continuity, 993 start bookend, 150 end bookend. Five independent instruments — band engine 16.9k floor, census conservation 18.9–22k, gate tracker, wide turnover 22–23.6k, geometric anchor 18–27k — converge on the same corridor, and the headline sits where the precise ones overlap. The end bookend is the line I'm proudest of: the engine said 1,813, my own screenshot audit said most of those people were already inside the last freeze, and I cut it to 150. A counting project where the owner never cuts his own number isn't a measurement, it's marketing.

### KeepItUp

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/keepitup
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: React 19, Anthropic + OpenAI + Gemini, Tree-sitter.

Self-hosted AI agent that auto-fixes broken deployments.

Self-hosted AI on-call agent. Polls six deploy platforms every five minutes, parses crashes with tree-sitter across six languages, drafts a fix through OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini, runs it past a confidence gate, and opens a PR — never pushes to main.

KeepItUp is an autonomous SRE agent that watches six deploy platforms 24/7 and tries to turn “page on call” into “review a PR after coffee.” The brain is a two-layer reasoning system: a tree-sitter AST walker indexes the offending file across six languages and feeds the model a 50-500 line context slice instead of the whole repo, and a separate Reviewer agent gates every proposed fix behind a confidence threshold. Fixes auto-PR only at ≥85% confidence, or ≥70% if a build verification passes — because verification is a stronger signal than a raw score. Three providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) sit behind a single LLM client with budget gates and cost telemetry, so swapping providers is a config change. The agent never pushes to main; it opens PRs, runs Semgrep + Trivy + Gitleaks scans in Docker, and rolls everything into a weighted 0-100 health score per repo. I built it because I wanted oncall to be a thing I review with coffee, not a thing that wakes me up.

### Ëndërrat e Mia

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/enderrat-e-mia
Year: 2026. Status: in-progress. Stack: Expo + RN, Claude Haiku + Flux, RevenueCat.

AI bedtime stories in Albanian, illustrated and read aloud.

Albanian-language bedtime stories, generated, illustrated, and narrated. Expo app on a Mongoose backend. Claude Haiku writes, fal.ai Flux Schnell paints four matched illustrations, TTS narrates, RevenueCat + AdMob fund the free tier, and an in-house pipeline renders the launch ad creatives.

Ëndërrat e Mia is an AI bedtime-story app for Albanian-speaking families — a market that essentially has zero native-language children's content, so parents end up translating Disney+ at bedtime. Each story is a three-step pipeline rendered atomically: Claude Haiku writes the narrative in Albanian, fal.ai's Flux Schnell paints four matched watercolor illustrations from the same character setup, and TTS narrates the whole thing — you never get orphaned text with missing audio. The most quietly proud move is the single Transaction ledger: free credits earned from ads, RevenueCat subscription credits, AdMob rewards, and one-off purchases all write to the same table, so balance, churn, and fraud queries are naturally unified instead of requiring three accounting systems. There's also a self-built programmatic ad-creative pipeline in `videos/generateAdImages*.js` — five scripts that render TikTok ad frames using the same children's-book watercolor styling as the in-app illustrations, so brand consistency is baked in. I shipped roughly thirty creatives for the launch this way, without a designer. I built it because my native-language community deserves bedtime stories that don't come from Google Translate.

### GymApp

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/gym-app
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: Express + Postgres, Socket.io + Redis, Expo + MUI.

White-label gym OS — NFC entry, member app, multi-tenant admin.

White-label gym OS for the Albanian market. Four deployables — admin web, member app, API, NFC scanner-bridge — sharing one branding record. Socket.io with a Redis adapter fans live occupancy across PM2 workers so every dashboard sees the same number.

GymApp is a white-label gym OS for the Albanian market — four independently deployable products that share one database and one branding record. The admin web, the member app, the API, and the NFC scanner-bridge all live in one monorepo; every Gym row stores its own primary color, logo, and bundle identifier, and at runtime the React Native member app reads `GymConfigContext` and *becomes* that gym's branded app. Live occupancy fans out across PM2 cluster workers via Socket.io with a Redis pub/sub adapter, so a tap at the turnstile reaches every dashboard, every member phone, every scanner — without polling. The scanner-bridge itself is a tiny `node-hid` service that reads card UIDs off a USB NFC reader and POSTs to `/api/visits`, decoupling hardware from the API entirely so a Raspberry Pi at the gate doesn't know any backend internals. Multi-tenancy is enforced by a `gymId` foreign key on every domain model plus middleware-scoped queries; super-admins can hop tenants. I also built a Remotion ad pipeline that renders TikTok creatives from the same React components used in the app — so the ad creative and the product UI literally cannot drift.

### Pilates Studio

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/pilates-studio
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: pnpm monorepo, Express + Prisma, Turso + libSQL.

Boutique studio platform — admin web, mobile app, API, 594 tests.

Branded studio platform — admin web, mobile app, API, 594 tests. Same Prisma schema runs on better-sqlite3 in dev and Turso (libsql) in prod via adapters. Express ships as a Vercel function with zero rewrites. Resend for email, Sentry for errors, Playwright for E2E.

Pilates Studio is a four-deployable platform for one boutique studio — the same Prisma schema runs on `better-sqlite3` in dev and Turso (libsql) in prod, swapped through the adapter pattern with zero code changes. Express ships as a Vercel serverless catch-all (`api/[[...path]].ts`), so the same code runs as a long-lived server locally and as edge functions in production. An audit middleware records every admin write — actor, resource, IP, user-agent — but never blocks the real operation if the audit insert fails, because losing a booking to a slow audit table is not an acceptable failure mode. 21 Prisma models, 594 tests across API + admin + mobile + Playwright E2E, transactional email through Resend with a graceful no-op when keys are missing. The booking flow has proper status transitions with auto-promotion from the waitlist on cancellation, so admins don't manually re-shuffle attendance. I built it because boutique studios get nickel-and-dimed by SaaS, and I wanted to prove a single solo dev could ship the same shape with discipline.

### CleanSlate

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/cleanslate
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: Next.js 16, Supabase + RLS, Telnyx + LemonSqueezy.

$20/month operating system for cleaning businesses.

$20/month operating system for solo cleaners in Germany. Next.js 16 with strict architecture: thin routes, services own data, Supabase RLS, money in cents, phones in E.164. Telnyx + WhatsApp for SMS, four Vercel cron endpoints, full German marketing site at the edge.

CleanSlate is a €20-flat operating system for solo cleaners in Germany — a discipline product disguised as a SaaS. Every architectural rule is enforced with no exceptions: route files dispatch to services, services own all data ops, components never touch Supabase, money is always cents, phones always E.164, RLS scopes every query to the user. The subscription expiry path is a pure RLS policy — when the trial runs out, no UI code runs; the database simply stops accepting INSERTs and the read-only state is automatic. Four Vercel cron endpoints handle trial reminders, overdue invoices, recurring job generation, and pre-job SMS, so the operator never logs in to do admin. Eleven services own the domain (billing, clients, earnings, invoices, jobs, profiles, search, SMS, WhatsApp, email, line items), and the full German marketing site — Datenschutz, Impressum, AGB, MDX-driven blog and ratgeber, a `/rechner` cost calculator — sits in a separate `(marketing)` route group from the authenticated `(app)`. I built it because the discipline *is* the product — you can't accidentally introduce a bug when components physically can't touch the database.

### Social Command Center

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/social-command-center
Year: 2026. Status: in-progress. Stack: Next.js 16, BullMQ + Drizzle, OpenAI + Postiz.

Industrial Instagram content for any brand — autonomous, multi-tenant.

Autonomous Instagram content factory for any brand. Drop a brand config + knowledge base, and a weekly BullMQ cron walks every brand through a 6-stage pipeline; posts auto-schedule via the Postiz API once images land. Three Claude Code slash commands give a zero-API-cost generation path that bypasses OpenAI entirely.

Social Command Center is an autonomous Instagram content factory for trade brands — adding a brand is a filesystem operation, not a code change. Each brand drops a JSON config plus a knowledge-base directory (brand DNA, customer ICP, voice), and a weekly BullMQ cron fires Mondays at 6 AM and walks every brand through a six-stage pipeline: Brand Discovery → Research → Strategy → Content Gen → Quality Gate → Post Creation, with retry/backoff and a real quality gate before anything reaches the calendar. Posts wait in `awaiting_image` until images are dragged into the dashboard, then auto-schedule via the Postiz REST API — a state machine, not a vibe. The cool unlock is the zero-API-cost path: three Claude Code slash commands (`/analyze-brand`, `/generate-content-plan`, `/generate-content`) read the knowledge base directly from disk and POST to `/api/import-content`, so I can generate twelve weeks of content for all seven brands without touching the OpenAI bill. I built it because seven brands times thirty posts a month is not a thing a human should be doing manually — and turning content generation into a deterministic, version-controlled pipeline made the agency-of-one model actually viable.

### Reel Farmer

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/reel-farmer
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: Bun + TS, Whisper + Gemini, Remotion + Puppeteer.

Self-hosted YouTube → TikTok pipeline. One command, multi-account.

Bun pipeline that turns YouTube into TikTok. yt-dlp downloads, Whisper transcribes, Gemini picks the clips, Remotion renders 1080×1920, stealth puppeteer uploads across multiple authenticated accounts. Resumable from any step. Companion Next.js dashboard reads the SQLite run database.

Reel Farmer is a self-hosted Bun pipeline that turns YouTube into TikTok shorts across multiple authenticated accounts — yt-dlp downloads, Whisper transcribes (configurable model size), Gemini picks the clips with the transcript in context, Remotion renders 1080×1920, stealth puppeteer uploads. Every stage writes to a deterministic `data/runs/<run-id>/` tree and stamps a SQLite checkpoint database, so `bun run resume <run-id>` skips finished work and picks up exactly where the last crash hit — long pipelines are inevitable, resumability is what makes them usable. The slideshow composer uses the same Remotion render pipeline as the captioned clips, so Pinterest-sourced slideshows and YouTube clips share a visual language. The multi-account uploader lives behind a single `account-manager.ts` API — cookie/session management, stealth puppeteer, and TikTok's compliance-flag dance all hidden behind one upload call. Trend and content scouts auto-discover what to clip rather than waiting for the operator to paste URLs. A separate Next.js dashboard reads the SQLite run database for status and queue management. I built it because I run a small media operation across multiple Albanian-themed accounts and a $30/month SaaS that doesn't do slideshows wasn't going to cut it.

### Dabei

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/dabei
Year: 2026. Status: in-progress. Stack: Expo + RN 0.83, Supabase + Realtime, react-native-maps.

Kiel's social pulse — find or start hangouts on a live map.

Kiel's social pulse — a live map of who's hanging out where, tonight. Expo + Supabase Realtime + react-native-maps. Vibe-checks let any hangout get live-rated mid-event. MMKV for hot-path caching, OTP auth, deep-link invites, persistent crews for repeat plans.

Dabei is a live social-pulse map of Kiel — a discovery layer for organic, in-person plans for the whole city, not a Meetup clone and not a dating app. The thing I'm most proud of is Vibe Checks as a first-class entity: a hangout can be live-rated mid-event, and the `submit_vibe_check` RPC enforces attendance proof and a 48-hour rating window before counting. Earn fifteen vibe checks from ten unique people and `profiles.is_trusted` flips automatically — reputation is built from shared experiences, not follower counts, so trust actually means something. The data layer is split into three services (`hangout-crud`, `hangout-queries`, `hangout-actions`) so reads, writes, and orchestrated business logic each have a clean boundary, which makes RLS reasoning local and testing actually targeted. MMKV replaces AsyncStorage on the cold-start hot path — synchronous and encrypted — so auth state and draft hangouts don't add async hops to first-launch time. I built it because Kiel's social life lives scattered across WhatsApp groups, Instagram DMs, and the StadtRadio bulletin — locals lose track of their own crews and newcomers have no way in.

### advance.al

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/projects/advance-al
Year: 2026. Status: shipped. Stack: React 18 + Vite, Express + MongoDB, OpenAI embeddings.

Albania's job marketplace — AI CV generation, AI profile-fill, embedding-ranked matching, auto-notify on match.

advance.al is Albania's job marketplace, with the AI layer doing real work end-to-end: jobseekers upload any CV (PDF or DOCX) and OpenAI structured-extraction auto-fills their profile; the platform also generates a branded Word-document CV in Albanian or English from that structured data. Every job and every candidate gets vector-embedded with text-embedding-3-small, then ranked with cosine similarity + a 7-dimension match score (title, skills, experience, location, education, salary, availability) + a bilingual category boost so old internships don't crowd current skills. Every new posting fans out automatic bilingual notifications via Resend to every matched user, with UTM tracking and one-click unsubscribe.

advance.al is Albania's job marketplace and the only project here with paying users from day one — three sides on one platform (jobseekers, employers, admins), each with their own dashboard. The AI layer does real work end-to-end: a jobseeker uploads any CV (PDF or DOCX), `pdfjs-dist` + `mammoth` extract the text, and OpenAI structured-extraction auto-fills the entire profile — skills, work history, education, contact, summary — so they're match-ready without typing a thing. The platform also generates a branded Word-document CV in Albanian or English from that same structured data using the `docx` library, with consistent colors and typography across the export. Matching combines two signals: every job and every profile gets vector-embedded with `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dims) for semantic ranking, and on top of cosine similarity sits a 7-dimension explainable score (title, skills, experience, location, education, salary, availability) — so the employer dashboard can show *why* a candidate scored 78 and not just the number. The third AI hook is the automatic notification fanout: every time an employer publishes a new job, an embedding worker recomputes matches and Resend sends a bilingual job-alert email to every qualified user with UTM tracking and a one-click unsubscribe token. The whole backend is Express 5 + MongoDB 8 with a Redis rate-limited OpenAI client, an embedding queue worker on its own heartbeat process, an alert system that emails me when drift crosses a threshold, GDPR retention crons that purge soft-deleted accounts after 30 days, and 288 Jest tests under a strict philosophy that bans permissive matchers and tautological assertions. The frontend is React 18 + Vite + Mantine + shadcn/ui, fully bilingual SQ/EN, with Playwright \"walker\" tests that screenshot every public + jobseeker + employer + admin route across desktop + iPhone 12 + Pixel 5 for every release. I learned how a marketplace actually works by running one.

## Notes (technical writeups)

### Two-layer reasoning for autonomous AI agents — how KeepItUp gates a fix before it PRs

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/keepitup-two-layer-reasoning
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

KeepItUp watches six deploy platforms 24/7 and tries to make oncall a thing the operator reviews with coffee instead of a thing that wakes them up. The interesting part isn't the watching — it's what the agent does in the gap between "build is broken" and "PR is open." It runs two LLM passes against the same problem, and the second one can veto the first.

The Generator pass uses a tree-sitter AST walker (same parser across six languages, after a v1 attempt with per-language regex got rolled back) to pull a 50-to-500-line slice around the symbol the stack trace points at — bounded in size, shape determined by the parse tree. Dense AST-slice context routinely beats whole-module dumps: shorter prompts are faster, cheaper, and produce fixes that don't accidentally rewrite adjacent helpers.

The Reviewer pass is a separate agent reading the diff cold — no chain-of-thought context from the Generator — scoring the proposed fix on a fresh axis: does this actually solve the stated problem, and does it introduce anything load-bearing that wasn't there. Both scores have to clear ≥85% confidence to open a PR. There's a relaxation rule: if build verification in a sandboxed container comes back green, the threshold drops to ≥70%, because a passing test suite is a stronger correctness signal than any model's self-report.

Three providers (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini) sit behind a single internal LLM client that owns provider selection, budget tracking, and per-call cost telemetry. The Generator/Reviewer split deliberately uses different providers to catch errors a single-model pipeline would miss — shared blind spots are the failure mode to avoid. Budget gates stop runaway agents from burning through credits when CI starts oscillating.

The agent never pushes to main. It opens PRs. Semgrep + Trivy + Gitleaks scans run against the diff in Docker before the PR opens. The whole stack rolls up to a per-repo health score from 0 to 100 — build status, deploy success rate, security findings, fix track record. Build the gate before the generator: the generator is the part that demos well, but the gate is the part that determines whether the agent is something you can actually run unattended.

### Resumable pipelines — how Reel Farmer survives a crash mid-render

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/reel-farmer-resumable-pipelines
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Reel Farmer is a self-hosted Bun pipeline that turns YouTube videos into TikTok shorts across multiple authenticated accounts — yt-dlp downloads, Whisper transcribes, Gemini picks clips, Remotion renders 1080×1920, stealth puppeteer uploads. The thing the design had to get right wasn't any individual stage; it was making sure a crash never cost more than the seconds since the last completed step.

Every run gets a UUID-shaped directory at `data/runs/<run-id>/`. Every artifact lands at a deterministic path inside it: `src/raw.mp4`, `src/transcript.json`, `clips/01.mp4`, `renders/01.vertical.mp4`, `uploads/01.metadata.json`. The path is the contract. Any tool that wants to operate on a stage's output knows where to look — no scanning, no indexing, no dashboards. `ls data/runs/<run-id>/` is a complete progress report.

Alongside the file tree sits a SQLite database with one row per (run-id, stage, status, timestamp, error). Status is one of `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`. Every stage's first act is to mark its row `running`. Every stage's last act is to mark it `completed` — or `failed` with a stack trace. `bun run resume <run-id>` reads this table, finds the first non-completed stage, and starts from there. Failed status carries a retry counter; after three retries the run is marked dead and stays dead until an operator looks.

The trick isn't catching exceptions and retrying within a stage. The trick is: every stage is a pure function of its inputs. If a stage crashed before completing, its output files are absent or partial. Resume just re-runs the stage; because the file paths are deterministic, the second attempt overwrites the first attempt's debris without cleanup logic. Idempotent stages plus deterministic paths equals resumable pipeline. The SQLite table is only the index; the file tree is the source of truth.

The design choice of SQLite over Redis or Postgres is deliberate: this pipeline runs on one box, no horizontal scaling story. SQLite gives ACID guarantees with zero deployment overhead. A crashed pipeline's full state is one `tar -cz` away from being inspected elsewhere. If it ever grew to multiple machines I'd swap SQLite for Postgres; the abstraction is one file and it's swappable.

A companion Next.js dashboard reads the SQLite run table and renders a per-run timeline. It writes nothing. The pipeline can crash, the dashboard keeps working. The dashboard can crash, the pipeline keeps working. The design rule: paths are contracts. If two stages need to coordinate, give them a deterministic file location to coordinate through.

### Vector embeddings for job-matching — why pure cosine similarity isn't enough

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/advance-al-vector-embeddings-job-matching
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

advance.al is Albania's job marketplace and the only project on this site with paying users from day one. The matching engine has to answer two questions for every job posted: which candidates are best for this job, and why. Pure cosine similarity over OpenAI embeddings handles the first. It falls apart on the second.

Every profile and every job gets vectorized with `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dimensions) at write time. The text is a normalized blob — title plus skills plus experience summary, and for jobs the responsibilities section. Albanian and English content live in the same vector space because the model handles both. Cosine similarity then ranks candidates against a job or jobs against a candidate. This is the easy half. Throw OpenAI's embedding API at it and you're done — assuming you don't mind your employer dashboard saying "candidate scored 0.83" with no explanation underneath.

On top of cosine, every match gets a seven-dimension breakdown: title match, skills match, experience match, location match, education match, salary fit, availability match. Each dimension is computed with its own rules — title is a normalized fuzzy match, skills use Jaccard against a controlled taxonomy, experience is a year-band overlap, location is a region/remote-status check, education matches degree levels, salary fit is range overlap, availability matches start-date windows. The employer dashboard can show "scored 78: title 32/40, skills 25/30, experience 12/15, location -1 (remote-only candidate, on-site role)" next to the candidate row.

Two layers let each one change independently. Cosine ranks; the dimension breakdown explains. Up-weighting skills relative to title is one weight change in the breakdown formula; the cosine ranking is untouched. It also means the recommendation can survive the next OpenAI embedding-model deprecation — `text-embedding-3-small` is the current default, and if it's replaced, cosine numbers will move but the dimension breakdown stays stable.

Every new job triggers an embedding worker on its own heartbeat process. The worker recomputes top-N matches and queues bilingual notifications through Resend. Each email has UTM tracking and a one-click unsubscribe token. Users get one email per matching job per day at most, deduped at the worker.

The change I'd make next: embed each section of a CV separately and average at query time, instead of one blob per profile. Long-form CVs lose nuance when flattened to 1536 dims. The fix is a schema change and a re-embedding pass — cheap compared to rebuilding the matching engine.

### Same schema, different databases — the Prisma adapter swap in Pilates Studio

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/prisma-adapter-swap-dev-prod-parity
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Pilates Studio runs better-sqlite3 in dev and Turso (libsql) in production. Same Prisma schema, same query code, same migration history. The adapter pattern handles the swap in two lines of config. This is the kind of dev/prod parity I used to fake with docker-compose; now I don't need to.

For most of its history Prisma was a closed system — one query engine, one wire protocol, one set of supported databases per engine. The adapter pattern decoupled the query engine from the connection: PrismaClient now accepts an `adapter` field that handles the actual database conversation. `@prisma/adapter-libsql` ships with libsql. `@prisma/adapter-better-sqlite3` ships with better-sqlite3. The schema and migrations are identical between them. The swap happens in one place — `src/lib/db.ts` returns the right adapter based on an env var.

The argument I used to hear was "just run Postgres in Docker locally." This works until someone's M-series Mac can't run the libpq image fast enough, or a teammate's connection limits don't match prod. The adapter pattern says: prod uses Turso (edge-replicated libsql), dev uses better-sqlite3 (in-process, no daemon). Both speak the same SQL dialect. Migrations apply identically. Schema diffs get caught at write time by the same Prisma validator. The dev pain is now zero — the database is a file in the repo's gitignore.

Pilates Studio's API ships as a Vercel serverless catch-all at `api/[[...path]].ts`. The same Express app runs as a long-lived server locally and as edge functions in production. The adapter swap is part of why this works — locally, the Express app keeps a single better-sqlite3 connection alive for its uptime; in production, each Vercel function invocation gets its own libsql client, which is fine because libsql connections are cheap and stateless. One codebase, two runtime models, zero rewrites.

The trade is a SQLite-dialect surface — no jsonb, no listen/notify, no range types. For an admin web plus mobile app plus booking API with 21 Prisma models, this is a non-issue. The full test surface (Vitest unit, supertest API integration, Playwright E2E for admin and mobile) runs against better-sqlite3. Production runs against Turso. The schema is the same. The migrations are the same. If a test passes locally, the prod behavior is one network hop different, not one database different.

### RLS as a subscription gate — letting Postgres turn off trial accounts for you

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/rls-subscription-gate-cleanslate
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

CleanSlate is a €20-flat operating system for solo cleaners in Germany. The subscription expiry path is the cleanest part of the codebase, because there is no path. When a user's trial runs out, the UI doesn't run a check; the database stops accepting INSERTs. The read-only state is automatic.

The usual approach to subscription gating is a `useEffect` on every authenticated page that checks if the user's subscription is active and redirects if not. This is a race-condition factory — the check runs after the page mounts, so for a few hundred milliseconds the UI shows the gated content. Every component that wants to do anything destructive needs its own check. And the database doesn't care. A clever user with the right knowledge could hit the API directly and write a row regardless of what the UI thinks.

CleanSlate moves the check to Supabase RLS. Every INSERT and UPDATE policy includes a clause like `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM subscriptions WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND status = 'active' AND current_period_end > NOW())`. When the period ends, the policy stops matching — INSERTs fail at the database, UPDATEs are blocked. SELECT is still allowed because the user can read their own data; they just can't change it. The UI doesn't need a single line of subscription-checking code. If a write fails, it fails the same way any RLS violation fails, and the existing error handling shows "your subscription has expired" instead of "you don't have permission."

The constraint is now adjacent to the data, not to the UI. Adding a new write endpoint doesn't risk forgetting the check. There's no race condition — the policy is evaluated at every query, in the same transaction as the write. A direct API call bypassing the UI gets the same treatment. There's no privileged path.

Subscription renewal happens through four Vercel cron endpoints — trial reminders, overdue invoices, recurring job generation, pre-job SMS. The operator never logs in to do admin. The crons run on a schedule, but if they don't run, the database state stays correct anyway, because the RLS policy doesn't depend on a job firing. LemonSqueezy webhooks update the `subscriptions` table when payments succeed. Telnyx sends SMS, Resend sends email. The database is the source of truth; everything else is glue.

The trade is commitment to Postgres plus RLS — switching to a NoSQL backend would be a rewrite, and RLS policies are harder to test in isolation than service-layer checks. The failure mode is also silent: if a policy is wrong, a write just fails, with no exception pointing at a missing check. I built CleanSlate as a discipline product. Every architectural rule is enforced with no exceptions, and RLS as a subscription gate is the same rule applied to time — the policy is the gate, not a UI check pretending to be one.

### Hiring a freelance full-stack engineer in Germany — a 2026 evaluation checklist

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/hiring-freelance-full-stack-engineer-germany-2026-checklist
Date: 2026-05-14. 9 min read.

Most checklists for hiring freelance engineers in Germany were written by recruiters who haven't shipped code in eight years. This is the one I wish more clients used: ask for a public repo and read the most recent commit diff (not a portfolio site); ask what they last broke and how they noticed (real engineers have stories about 3am Sentry alerts and Supabase RLS policies written backwards); verify they ship with tests, not screenshots (594 tests in Pilates Studio, 288 in advance.al — verifiable numbers, not "I write tests where appropriate"); check that they own the deploy, not just the code (a freelancer who only owns the code means you're now the DevOps team).

The two German-market specifics nobody warns clients about: Scheinselbständigkeit (disguised employment — the Deutsche Rentenversicherung can retroactively classify your freelancer as an employee if they work exclusively for you, on your premises, with your equipment, on your schedule — mitigate via multiple clients, deliverable-based contracts, freelancer's own equipment); Stundensatz vs Werkvertrag (hourly rate vs fixed-deliverable contract — pick the one that matches how clearly the work can be defined upfront).

Quick filter table — green flags vs red flags: public recent commits vs outdated boilerplate; specific test count + CI badge vs "I write tests where appropriate"; owns deploy end-to-end vs hands off git push; specific incident story with root cause vs "I don't really break things"; asks scoping questions before quoting vs quotes immediately; multiple clients + deliverable-based vs hourly + single client full-time.

Every project on this portfolio is solo across stack, with public repos where possible, tests in CI, security scans in deploy pipelines (Semgrep + Trivy + Gitleaks in KeepItUp), and deploys owned end-to-end. The case studies exist specifically so evaluation can happen against real work rather than against a deck.

### Hiring a freelance Next.js developer — 7 questions that filter the field

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/hiring-freelance-nextjs-developer-7-questions
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Most Next.js freelancers list "Next.js, React, Tailwind" on their profile and have shipped exactly one tutorial app. Seven questions, five minutes each, that separate people who've shipped Next.js production code from people who haven't:

(1) App Router vs Pages Router — which would you pick today and why? Real answer engages with trade-offs (App Router for nested layouts and Server Components but harder legacy migration; Pages Router for getServerSideProps semantics and a long stable surface). (2) When do you reach for a Client Component instead of a Server Component? Client for event handlers, browser APIs, hooks, third-party libs that touch window; Server for data-fetching, secrets, non-interactive rendering. (3) How do you handle data fetching at the edge? Should mention edge constraints, Fluid Compute, regional pinning, latency-to-user vs latency-to-database trade. (4) What's your CSP look like for a real app? Should mention blob: in script-src for Web Workers, connect-src for third-party APIs, worker-src for explicit worker permissions — these matter on any Three.js / R3F / Lottie app. (5) How do you ship a sitemap? Next 16 has a built-in sitemap.ts convention; a Next.js dev should mention MetadataRoute.Sitemap. (6) ISR vs SSG vs SSR vs Edge — when each? Sweet-spot recall: SSG for known build-time content, ISR for revalidation-on-write content, SSR for per-request personalized, Edge for latency-dominated routes. (7) Worst Next.js gotcha you've hit in production? Specific stories — hydration mismatch, Server Component pulling in client-only package, middleware redirect loop, CSP block on blob worker, image-optimization quota.

The candidates worth hiring are the ones who push back on at least one question — they're engaging with the framework as a real tool, not as bullet points on their CV.

### Hiring a freelance AI engineer in 2026 — portfolio red flags and green flags

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/hiring-freelance-ai-engineer-2026-portfolio-flags
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Half the freelance "AI engineers" wrapped one OpenAI API call in a Streamlit app and called themselves senior. The portfolio tells you which half you're talking to in five minutes.

Red flags: a single Streamlit/Gradio demo app with no production deployment (demos are easy; production AI is the code around the model call — validation, prompt versioning, retries, observability, budgeting); no mention of model failure modes (production engineers talk about hallucinations, prompt injection, output drift, model deprecation constantly); claims about AGI or "general intelligence" (anyone using those phrases is selling vibes — production AI work is small, specific, unglamorous); no cost telemetry or budget gates (a freelancer who hasn't tracked per-call cost hasn't shipped at scale).

Green flags: multi-provider routing (Anthropic Claude for code reasoning, OpenAI GPT-4-class for different blind spots, Gemini for budget overflow — KeepItUp routes per-stage, not per-app); specific failure-mode storytelling ("my structured-extraction prompt worked on 99% of CVs until a one-page H1-only PDF, the model invented an entire work history, I added length check + confidence threshold + manual-review fallback"); evaluation framework not vibes (advance.al has held-out manually-labeled candidate/job pairs and 288 Jest tests with banned permissive matchers and tautological assertions); owns the model-failure recovery (when the model returns nonsense, what happens — retry, fallback, human-in-loop).

Provider routing maturity table: single provider hardcoded (demo-tier) → single provider abstracted (beginning) → multi-provider per task (production-tier) → multi-provider plus budget gates (senior production-tier).

The senior AI engineers are the ones who talk about what their AI can't do at least as much as what it can. They've felt the edges. They build for the failure mode, not the demo mode.

### Tree-sitter AST slicing as a context-budget lever for AI agents

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/tree-sitter-ast-slicing-context-budget
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Token budgets are a real constraint for AI agents working on source code. A 30,000-token "here's the whole module" dump performs worse than a 3,000-token AST-shaped slice. Models are sharper when context is dense — needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks measure recall not reasoning, and a model that can pull a fact out of 100K tokens isn't the same as one that can reason about that fact when 99% of surrounding tokens are noise.

Naive regex-based slicing breaks down fast (nested closures with string-literal braces, indentation-based blocks, six languages with six different grammars). Tree-sitter parses source into a real concrete syntax tree — function definitions, class declarations, imports, control-flow blocks — all addressable as tree nodes with parent/sibling relationships intact. The same query API works across every grammar. One slicer, dozens of languages. Written in C, incremental, single-digit-millisecond parses on thousand-line files.

KeepItUp targets 50-to-500-line slices. Below 50, the model starts inferring; above 500, noise-to-signal ratio hurts. The slice grows from the failing function outward — enclosing function plus the imports it references, type declarations the signature uses, sibling methods called from the failing function, the module-level docstring. Deliberate exclusions: other-file code (separate concern), commented-out code, generated boilerplate (file-header heuristics), unrelated code.

The slice interacts with the confidence gate: if context is missing, the Generator's diff references the missing function as if it doesn't exist, the Reviewer scores low, the diff doesn't open a PR. The system fails closed — wrong slice means low confidence means no action. The slice is part of the safety story, not just an optimization.

The pattern generalizes: if the input has a grammar, use the grammar. Markdown agents slice by heading; Kubernetes-manifest agents slice by resource; HCL-config agents slice by block. The amount of context an LLM can use effectively is bounded; the grammar tells you which bounded slice to pick.

### Three-model atomic content pipelines — text, image, and audio without orphans

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/three-model-atomic-content-pipelines
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Ëndërrat e Mia generates each bedtime story by composing three different models — Claude Haiku for Albanian text, fal.ai Flux Schnell for four matched watercolor illustrations, ElevenLabs for narration. None of the three is allowed to land alone. A half-generated story is worse than no story, because the user has lost a credit and gained nothing.

Pipeline shape: Step 1 — Claude Haiku writes title + 10-paragraph narrative in Albanian + 4 illustration scene descriptions. Step 2 — pipeline sends those 4 descriptions to Flux Schnell with a fixed watercolor-style prefix and the same character description (visual consistency). Step 3 — ElevenLabs narrates the full text; pipeline checks audio duration against expected reading time (~150 words/minute Albanian) and rejects out-of-range output. Only after all three pass validation does the pipeline commit the story to the user's library.

Why three different providers: no single one does all three best. Albanian text on Anthropic Haiku (strong on low-resource languages, noticeably better than equivalent-price OpenAI / Gemini output); watercolor-style image consistency on Flux Schnell (cheap, fast, style consistency across multi-image generation holds up under the character-continuity constraint); Albanian TTS on ElevenLabs (voice quality meaningfully ahead of competitors for Albanian at the time of build). Three providers means three rate limits, three pricing curves, three failure modes — but the alternative is accepting weaker output on at least one stage.

Transaction ledger underneath: free credits from ads, RevenueCat subscription credits, AdMob rewards, one-off purchases all write to the same `transactions` table. Balance is a single SUM query; refunds are positive-amount rows referencing the original debit. The pipeline's atomic commit shows up here too — if the story commits, the debit stays; if any stage fails, a refund row writes immediately. User never sees a debit without either a story or a refund.

Failure recovery: each stage has up to three retries with slightly modified prompts before the pipeline gives up. Failures aren't logged as user-facing problems until retries exhaust. Result: roughly 99% of attempts succeed; the 1% that don't are auto-refunded and surface as ops alerts, not customer-support tickets.

Pattern generalizes to any multi-model AI feature: orchestrate stages, validate every output, refuse to commit unless all pass, refund automatically on failure. Pipeline owns the transaction; models don't have to know about each other.

### Hiring a freelance React Native developer in Germany — a scope template

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/hiring-freelance-react-native-developer-germany
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

React Native projects fail on scope, not skill. Before hiring, define: target platforms (iOS, Android, web?), Expo managed vs bare workflow, native modules required, deploy strategy (EAS / App Store Connect / Google Play), offline-first requirements. These five answers change the estimate by an order of magnitude.

Platform choice — iOS-only is cheapest to develop, most expensive to maintain. Android-only has broader reach but more device fragmentation. Both means double the testing matrix. React Native Web adds another testing dimension; most apps don't need it. Workflow — Expo managed is the right call for ~80% of projects (EAS Build + EAS Submit, no local Xcode/Android Studio for normal feature work). Bare is for projects with native modules Expo doesn't support, slower development experience. Native modules — 0-2 fits tight scope; 3-5 doubles estimate; 6+ is native-team territory. Deploy — confirm the freelancer owns EAS + App Store Connect + Google Play end-to-end, including TestFlight beta cycle. Offline-first — yes/no changes architecture; offline requires MMKV/SQLite + conflict resolution + queue-and-replay, adds 4-6 weeks.

Dabei (Kiel social-pulse app on this portfolio, in progress) is the worked example: Expo Router 5 on RN 0.83, Supabase + Realtime, react-native-maps, MMKV for hot-path caching, OTP auth, deep-link invite flow, three-services data layer for clean RLS reasoning.

### Hiring a freelance Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central contractor in Germany — what to evaluate

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/freelance-business-central-d365-germany-contractor
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Business Central freelancers split into three tiers — config-only (UI navigation, basic reports, €60-90/hour), AL-extension developers (custom tables/pages/codeunits/reports, €90-130/hour), full-stack (AL + REST/OAuth2 integrations + NAV→BC migrations, €120-180/hour). Most German SMBs migrating off NAV need tier three; most freelance profiles claim tier three; ratio of claim-to-reality is ~4:1.

Tell which tier you're talking to: ask for an AL extension code sample (tier-1 deflects, tier-2 shows a small extension, tier-3 walks through event subscriptions + upgrade compatibility patterns); ask about OAuth2 token refresh flow ("OAuth2 is a frontend thing" is disqualifying); ask about one real NAV→BC migration with specifics (data volume, custom tables carried, what went wrong, duration). German-market overlays: DATEV export for tax-advisor handoff, GoBD compliance for audit trails, ELSTER tax interface, Datenschutz / data-minimization configuration. Tier-3 contractors working in Germany know these by name.

Where to find tier-3 contractors: Microsoft Partner Center directory (skews toward agencies), Microsoft Tech Community + BCTechDays presenters, GitHub (search for AL extensions on real profiles), personal portfolios that show actual projects. Microsoft Business Central is on the skills track at this portfolio — AL extensions and REST/OAuth2 integrations for SMBs migrating from NAV.

### Freelance vs agency for a software MVP — a 2026 comparison

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/freelance-vs-agency-software-mvp-2026
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Solo experienced freelance engineer wins when scope is clear, one decision-maker exists, project fits one person's working memory (≤4 months), stack the freelancer has shipped before, no regulatory complexity. Solo wins on speed-of-iteration — no internal coordination tax, deployed change by lunch on morning feedback. Agency wins when work splits into parallel streams (custom design + backend + mobile simultaneously), timeline 6+ months, formal compliance overhead, continuity guarantees needed.

Cost comparison — senior full-stack freelancer at €100-150/hour on a 3-month MVP delivers €60K-€100K project cost; equivalent agency engagement lands €120K-€250K because you're paying for PM + designer + backend + frontend + QA + overhead. Agency premium pays for parallelism + process; whether worth it depends on whether you need those. Hybrid models: solo freelancer + part-time designer (20% time); solo freelancer + part-time QA pass; agency for discovery/architecture phase + solo for execution. Most MVPs don't need agency premium.

Before signing — solo: walk me through three projects you've shipped solo end-to-end (requirements, deploy, monitoring, support); agency: tell me who'll actually do the work (names, GitHub, hourly availability) because many agencies pitch with seniors and deliver with juniors.

### Solo developer vs team of three — when each ships faster

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/solo-developer-vs-team-of-three-when-each-ships-faster
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Coordination overhead grows non-linearly with team size — Brooks's Law applies even at small scale. Two people coordinate over coffee; three need a standup; four need a Slack channel and weekly sync; five need a project manager. Three engineers add ~2.2x execution but ~3x coordination (standups + PR reviews + design syncs + conflict resolution).

Solo wins on projects that fit one person's working memory (~4 months), one decision-maker, tightly-integrated full-stack work. Three wins on parallel streams (native iOS + native Android + backend), long projects (6+ months with continuity risk), formal compliance overhead, 24/7 oncall coverage. Hidden cost of team-of-three for MVPs — more code than one person produces, but more code isn't more value; codebases grow complexity to accommodate parallel work (more abstractions, more interfaces, more configuration), visible "design by committee" patterns six months in.

Concrete hiring test: if a candidate engineer can sketch your project's full architecture on a whiteboard in 20 minutes, the project fits one person. If it takes 90 minutes and three diagrams, you probably need a team.

### Where to find freelance software developers in Germany — 2026 guide

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/where-to-find-freelance-software-developers-germany-2026
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Six channels ranked by signal quality:

(1) Personal portfolios with public case studies — best signal, hardest to find. Google specific stack + "freelance" + Germany; the pages with real case studies (not just contact forms) are the start. No platform tax; do screening yourself. (2) GitHub profile-driven outreach — high signal, low platform tax. Browse repos in your stack with recent commits + clear docs; look for Germany-based devs; reach out directly. Most maintainers of real public repos are open to freelance even if they don't advertise. (3) Toptal / Malt — pre-vetted, ~15-25% margin. Toptal is broader/international; Malt is Europe-focused with strong Germany presence. Trade screening time for margin. (4) freelance.de / Freelancermap — German-market dominance, mixed quality. Strong for SAP / BC / NAV / ABAP enterprise contractors; weaker for modern web stacks. (5) LinkedIn direct outreach — mixed signal. Use Boolean searches for niche specialties; cold response rates 5-15%; tailor every message. (6) Upwork / Fiverr — cheapest, lowest signal. Quality candidates exist but require significant screening effort; not recommended for ongoing trust.

For senior full-stack: start with personal portfolios, expand to GitHub outreach, then Malt if no match in two weeks. For specialty work (BC/SAP/NAV): freelance.de + Microsoft Partner Center. Avoid mass-blasting Upwork postings.

### The freelance developer due-diligence checklist — code, tests, deploys, security

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/freelance-developer-due-diligence-checklist
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

20-minute technical pass that catches the bottom 80% of bad freelance hires. Four categories:

(1) Code — open most recent commit diff. Looking for focused changes (~10-100 lines, not 2000+), clear messages, code that does one thing well. Filter out generated boilerplate, "Update README.md" with no content, monolithic commits. Read 3-4 recent commits to see how this person works day-to-day.

(2) Tests — CI badges (GitHub Actions / Codecov), specific test counts in project descriptions ("594 tests across Vitest + Playwright"). Run their `pnpm test` if open. Watch for test theater (one trivial test to pass the badge check).

(3) Deploys — which platform (Vercel/Render/Fly/AWS/VPS), env-var management, deploy-failure recovery, error notification. Concrete signals: live deploys you can access, named monitoring tools (Sentry, Vercel Analytics), rollback story. Red flag: "I hand off the code and the client handles deployment."

(4) Security — CSP in deployed app, pre-commit secret-scanning hooks, dependency-update workflow (Dependabot/Renovate). Ask: how do you rotate a production secret if it leaks? What does your CI scan for? Tier-3 freelancers run Semgrep + CodeQL + Trivy + Gitleaks; tier-1 run nothing.

Across the 10 projects on this portfolio: every one has documented deploys, tests in CI (or clear architectural reason not), and sensitive-data projects (CleanSlate, advance.al) have RLS policies + audit trails as architectural primitives.

### Freelance vs Festanstellung — a 2026 reality check for software engineers in Germany

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/freelance-vs-festanstellung-2026-germany
Date: 2026-05-14. 8 min read.

Gross numbers mislead. A senior software engineer in Germany sees freelance at €100/hour and employed at €80-100K/year — naive math says 1.8x advantage. Real math: freelancers bill 1,400-1,500 effective hours (after admin time, client gaps, sick days, vacation, scope calls), landing at €140-150K. Subtract: private Krankenversicherung €5-10K/year, no paid vacation (~€10K equivalent loss), no employer pension contribution, no sick pay, Scheinselbständigkeit insurance, accountant. After all that, freelance break-even vs €80-100K Festanstellung is ~1.5-1.8x gross — meaningful but not the 2-3x mirage.

Freelance wins on flexibility (six-week summer break no negotiation), ceiling (10-20% annual rate growth possible), variety (rotate problems/stacks), tax structure (legitimate business expense deductions). Festanstellung wins on stability (Kündigungsschutz after six months), floor (statutory minimum protections), pension (statutory contributions built in), mental load (no pipeline / invoice / contract / tax overhead).

Scheinselbständigkeit (disguised employment) — Deutsche Rentenversicherung can retroactively classify a freelance relationship as employment if structure looks like employment (single client, on premises, with equipment, on schedule). Practical mitigations: Werkvertrag (deliverable contracts), multiple clients, demonstrated ability to take other work.

### Build verification beats raw confidence — why test suites outweigh self-reports

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/build-verification-beats-raw-confidence-scores
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

A test suite is a stronger correctness signal than any LLM's self-confidence. KeepItUp's gate opens a PR at ≥85% Generator + Reviewer confidence by default. With build verification (run the proposed diff through the test suite in a sandboxed Docker container) and a green result, the threshold drops to ≥70%. A diff that passes 200 tests at 70% confidence beats a diff that fails three tests at 90% confidence, every time.

Why model confidence alone fails — both Generator and Reviewer passes can share blind spots; a syntactically clean diff that compiles + passes the model's reasoning check can break behavior the test suite covers explicitly. Without verification, that PR makes the review queue; with it, confidence flips below threshold and the agent doesn't act. Thresholds are tuned empirically against historical CI failures + held-out fix-correctness sample. Below 70% with verification: false positives jump (low-confidence diffs subtly wrong in ways tests don't catch). Above 85% without verification: acceptable for unattended PR creation but conservative.

What if the repo has no tests — lint + type-check count as weak verification (catches syntactic, not semantic), threshold stays at 85%, no relaxation earned. Right fix is adding tests, not lowering threshold. Pattern generalizes — any AI agent taking action with cost benefits from verifying proposal against ground truth before acting; threshold reflects which signals are available.

### Multi-provider routing — running Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini behind one client

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/multi-provider-routing-anthropic-openai-gemini
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Single-provider LLM stacks are fragile. KeepItUp routes between Anthropic Claude (Generator: code reasoning + uncertainty calibration), OpenAI GPT-4-class (Reviewer: different blind spots; structured extraction), and Google Gemini (fallback: cheaper per token) behind one internal client. Routing isn't load-balancing — it's pairing different models on stages so they don't share blind spots. Same prompt through two Claude instances is closer to 1.5 passes than 2.

Client API: `llmClient.complete({ stage, prompt, schema, budget })`. Stage is the routing key; everything else hidden. Schema enforcement via Zod on every response with backoff retry on validation failure. Budget gates per (tenant, time-bucket, stage) — once exhausted, calls refused, agent stops proposing fixes (keeps watching). Cost telemetry per call: provider, model, stage, tokens, latency, USD cost, trace ID. Outage handling: fallback provider with short backoff; outage telemetry logs events + emits Slack alert.

Pattern generalizes — any production AI feature calling more than one LLM ought to do this. Hard-coding `OpenAI.chat.completions.create(...)` throughout the codebase is the pattern that makes you eat the next migration whole.

### Cost telemetry per LLM call — what to actually measure

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/cost-telemetry-per-llm-call-what-to-measure
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Per call: provider, model, stage, input + output tokens, latency, cost USD, trace ID, timestamp. Eight fields. At 100K calls/month, hundreds of MB — trivial to store, queryable in any time-series database. Aggregations: daily spend per tenant, daily spend per stage, cost per successful action (PR opened, match generated, story rendered), cost per failed vs successful attempt (failures usually cost more — retries). Monthly trend at constant volume catches prompt regressions inflating input.

Anomaly detection: daily spend > 3σ above trailing 30-day average emails me. Single-call cost > $1 USD emits event (LLM call rarely should cost a dollar; usually means unexpected context or runaway generation). Tenant exceeding 50% over monthly budget triggers hard-stop; 80% triggers less alarmist alert. What not to do: don't store full prompts and responses by default (expensive + often sensitive — capture hash for dedup analysis, leave bodies out unless debug mode); don't aggregate too aggressively before storing (raw events cheap to roll up; pre-aggregated rollups impossible to drill down from).

### Why an AI agent should run Semgrep, Trivy, and Gitleaks before opening a PR

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/semgrep-trivy-gitleaks-pre-pr-docker
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Anyone who's run an LLM at scale has seen a model regenerate code that originally had an API key inlined. Three security scans run in a sandboxed Docker container against every proposed diff: Semgrep (static analysis — SQL injection, hardcoded credentials, unsafe deserialization, language-specific anti-patterns); Trivy (dependency vulnerability scanner against CVE databases); Gitleaks (secret detection — regex + entropy heuristics for API keys, JWT secrets, AWS keys).

Any scanner flag adds a comment to the PR + `security-review-required` label, but doesn't block opening. Two reasons: false positives are real (Semgrep flags patterns that might be intentional in context; Gitleaks flags high-entropy strings that might be test fixtures); the agent's value is reducing my review work, not eliminating it (flagging without blocking respects the boundary — agent does the scan + writeup, I make the judgment call). Pattern generalizes to any AI agent proposing changes that will run in production — agent proposes, deterministic checks gate, human reviews what's left.

### Polling six deploy platforms 24/7 — API patterns that don't get rate-limited

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/polling-six-deploy-platforms-without-rate-limit-hell
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Webhooks first (GitHub Actions, Vercel, most production CI/CD platforms). Thin Next.js webhook handler drops events into a queue; downstream workers pick them up. Adaptive polling for platforms without webhooks: 60s during recent activity, 5min during business-hours quiet, 30min off-hours. Adaptive cuts request volume by 80%+ vs naive constant polling.

Exponential backoff on 429 and 5xx — double interval up to cap, single probe after backoff, double again if still failing. Cache deploy-status responses with platform-tuned TTLs (Vercel 30s, Render 1-3min). Share a global token bucket across worker processes via Redis-backed counter (single Redis instance serves bucket + cache + pub/sub queue). If a platform rate-limits anyway, the right response is poll less, not switch IPs — the agent works around rate limits, doesn't fight them.

The number of AI agent projects retrying on 1-second loops until success is too many. Tight retry loops are how you get IP-banned by a deploy platform.

### Stealth puppeteer and multi-account uploaders — the TikTok compliance-flag dance

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/stealth-puppeteer-multi-account-tiktok-compliance
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

TikTok bot detection looks at three categories — browser fingerprint (user agent, WebGL signatures, navigator properties, fonts), behavioral patterns (mouse movement, typing cadence, time-on-page), session signals (cookie age, IP reputation, time-of-day, request frequency). Vanilla puppeteer fails on fingerprint immediately (`navigator.webdriver = true`, "HeadlessChrome" UA, default WebGL signature). puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth patches the obvious tells.

Cookie management per account — never share jars, never reuse after fingerprint change, refresh on every successful upload. account-manager.ts API: `accountManager.upload(accountSlug, file, metadata)` hides cookie load + puppeteer launch + behavioral interaction + upload + cookie persist + browser close. Behavioral patterns matter as much as fingerprint — humanize() helper wrapping clicks (50-200ms randomized delays), scrolls, typing (variable cadence, bursty not 5 chars/second exact). Residential proxies only needed for high-volume or flagged-account recovery scenarios. Never automate a personal account you care about.

### Remotion video rendering with the same components as the app — brand consistency without two codebases

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/remotion-programmatic-video-rendering-app-components
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Remotion is React-based offline video rendering — components describe each frame, composition has duration + frame rate, headless Chromium renders MP4/WebM. The trick: import components from `packages/ui` in both your app workspace and your `apps/ads` workspace. A button rendered in the app and a button rendered in an ad share one source of truth.

Where Remotion shines: 15-90 second social-media clips, programmatic carousels, data-driven explainers, ad creative regenerated weekly with different content. Where it struggles: interactivity, very long durations, sub-frame audio sync. Reel Farmer's slideshow composer + captioned-clip renderer share visual language. Ëndërrat ad pipeline renders TikTok ad frames using the same children's-book watercolor styling as in-app illustrations.

Right call: After Effects for hero-level brand films; Remotion for everyday ad creative where consistency-with-the-app matters more than animation richness.

### Whisper model size — when bigger isn't worth the GPU

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/whisper-model-size-when-bigger-isnt-worth-it
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Six Whisper sizes — tiny (39M), base (74M), small (244M), medium (769M), large-v3 (1550M), large-v3-turbo. Quality gap isn't linear: tiny→base is big, base→small meaningful, small→medium smaller, medium→large incremental. For transcript-as-input-to-LLM (Reel Farmer's clip-selection use case), base or small is usually right — 80-90% as accurate as large at 10-30x speed. The downstream clip-selection LLM is robust to minor transcription errors.

User-facing transcripts (captions, legal review) need medium/large because every word matters. Multilingual content needs medium minimum — Whisper's accuracy on non-English drops faster with smaller models. OpenAI Whisper API: ~$0.006/minute regardless of size; self-hosted on $0.50/hour cloud GPU: large transcribes one hour of audio in ~6 minutes ($0.05); tiny in ~30 seconds ($0.004). Crossover for API vs self-host: ~100 hours/month. Reel Farmer's default: base for English, medium for non-English, large-v3 on explicit request.

### Gemini clip selection — getting an LLM to pick highlights with the transcript in context

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/gemini-clip-selection-transcript-context
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Gemini's long context window (1M+ tokens) makes it the right model for clip selection from full podcast transcripts. Prompt structure: (1) full transcript with timestamps, (2) criteria for what makes a good clip (surprising claims, complete arguments, sharp one-liners, anything that holds attention without context), (3) output schema (JSON array of `{ startSec, endSec, summary, confidence }`). `responseMimeType: 'application/json'` enforces structure; schema-validation failures get one retry with stricter framing.

Heuristics filter bad picks — length bounds (15-60s), confidence threshold (deprioritize <0.7), overlap merging (clips overlapping >50% become one), total cap (top 7 per run). Operator reviews dashboard, marks approved clips for render. Selection review is the one intentional human-in-loop step because difference between "AI thinks this is good" and "this is actually good" is real, and 30s per clip is cheap insurance against bad picks training the algorithm against the channel.

Empirically Gemini and Claude perform similarly on this task, both beat GPT-4 by a meaningful margin (rankings shift with each model release; benchmark for your use case).

### The transaction ledger — unifying ads, subscriptions, and purchases into one accounting story

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/transaction-ledger-unified-credits-mobile-app
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Ëndërrat e Mia's billing has four sources — RevenueCat subscriptions, AdMob rewards, in-app purchases, free trial — all writing to one Transaction table. Columns: id, user_id, amount (positive credit, negative debit), source (revenuecat / admob / iap / story_render / refund / promo), external_id (subscription ID, reward ID, purchase token, or null for system-internal), created_at, notes. Balance = `SELECT SUM(amount) FROM transactions WHERE user_id = ?`. No state machine. No reconciliation. The balance is whatever the rows say it is.

When a story is requested, the pipeline writes a debit row before generation starts. If any stage fails, a refund row writes (referencing the debit). The user's net balance is restored automatically — no race conditions, no orphaned debits. Webhook handlers per source validate signatures + insert one row each (external_id uniqueness enforced at DB level so replayed webhooks are no-op, not duplicate credit).

Fraud queries become single queries: "users who got unusual admob credit in 24h" = one SELECT against one table. Compare to four-tables-stitched-together version with three joins + edge cases per source. Table is append-only — cancellations and refunds are new rows, not deletions (same discipline as double-entry bookkeeping). At very high volume, partition by month; Postgres handles natively, query API unchanged.

### Embedding worker on a heartbeat process — the pattern that keeps a matching engine honest

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/embedding-worker-heartbeat-process-pattern
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

advance.al's embedding worker runs on its own PM2 process (cluster mode runs N web workers + 1 embedding worker). Every 60s the worker pings a heartbeat endpoint with timestamp + identity; cron job every 5min checks recency; >10min silent triggers alert email + Slack. The whole monitoring layer is ~30 lines of code and catches the silent-stop failure mode where the platform appears working but matches stop updating.

PM2's `online` status catches crashes but not hangs (process running and not making progress — blocked on network call, stuck on lock, pegged on CPU without useful work). Heartbeat catches hangs. Both signals together cover the failure surface. Worker pops jobs from Redis queue: fetch entity, generate embedding via `text-embedding-3-small`, store via pgvector, recompute downstream matches if significant change. Failure handling: retry counter, dead-letter after 3 retries + alert. Common modes: OpenAI rate limits (backoff recover), Postgres connection drops (reconnect), validation errors (log + skip).

Pattern generalizes to any background worker critical to product function — notification fanouts, image processors, index rebuilders. Cost: 30 lines + one cron + one alert channel. Benefit: 10-minute detection vs days-later user complaints.

### OpenAI structured extraction — auto-filling profiles from any CV format

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/openai-structured-extraction-profile-autofill
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Three pieces stitched together: (1) text extraction (pdfjs-dist for PDFs, mammoth for DOCX — returns single long string of CV content); (2) structured LLM extraction (OpenAI Chat API + `responseMimeType: 'application/json'` + explicit schema describing fields — name, email, phone, skills, work_history, education, summary, all with per-field confidence); (3) confidence routing (fields above 0.7 silently auto-fill, below trigger manual-review UI).

Structured output is categorical, not incremental. Free-form parsing of "extract this person's skills" returns inconsistent shapes (comma-separated, bulleted, sentence describing). Structured output returns guaranteed-valid JSON every time. The feature is feasible because the API exists; without it, validation + retry would be most of the code.

Image-only PDF handling: pdfjs-dist returns empty strings on rasterized pages. Detection: <100 chars total = treat as image-PDF. Fallback: OCR via Tesseract or OpenAI vision (more expensive but handles edge case; <5% of uploads). Edge case fix: one-page PDF with single H1 made the model invent an entire work history; length check at start of pipeline now refuses uploads under 100 chars.

Pattern generalizes to any user-facing form where input is unstructured and destination is typed — receipt scanning, invoice extraction, lease-agreement parsing.

### Bilingual embeddings and the category boost — when one vector space isn't enough

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/bilingual-embedding-category-boost
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

Modern OpenAI embeddings handle multilingual content in one shared 1536-dim vector space. But vocabulary depth differs by language — model has seen orders of magnitude more English technical writing than Albanian technical writing. Result: an Albanian-only profile matching an English-only job scores lower than the candidate's qualifications justify, because Albanian semantic neighborhoods are thinner.

Observed bias (held-out matched pair set): English-mixed profile vs English job 0.78 cosine baseline; Albanian-only vs English 0.62 (23% application rate lower); Albanian-only vs Albanian 0.79 baseline; English-mixed vs Albanian 0.68 (12% lower). Fix: coarse-category tag on every profile and job (Software Engineering, Marketing, Sales, etc., mutually exclusive at top level). When candidate + job share top-level category, cosine gets small additive boost (+0.05 to +0.08). Same category in different languages now ranks closer to same category in same language; cross-category matches unaffected.

Why categories not language detection: stable signal regardless of bilingual content classification ambiguity; doesn't require per-language scaling factors to retune on every OpenAI model release. Result after shipping: Albanian-only application rates against English-language listings up ~18% in first month; employer-reported candidate quality unchanged.

Pattern generalizes to any multilingual matching engine where one language has shallower training data, or any cross-domain matching where same-domain matches deserve a boost.

### Drift detection in a vector matching engine — when the model has changed

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/drift-detection-vector-matching-engine
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

OpenAI deprecates embedding models. ada-002 → 3-small → 3-large. Every migration is a re-embedding pass + cosine number shift. A matching engine without drift detection discovers the change when employers complain about new candidates appearing in their dashboard.

Drift signal: per-candidate top-N match-list stability. Daily job picks stratified sample of 200 candidates; computes top-5 matches; compares against last week's top-5; computes Jaccard turnover. Baseline: trailing 30-day average. Threshold: anything >2× baseline triggers alert with affected candidates + change pattern + investigation dashboard link. First action: check OpenAI version. Second: verify embedding worker. Third: look for content shifts (new categories, new geographies).

The 7-dimension explainable score on top of cosine (title, skills, experience, location, education, salary, availability) protects dashboard UX — dimension formulas don't depend on embedding model. Cosine numbers shift after migration; dimension breakdowns stay stable; user-visible "candidate scored 78" doesn't make employers think the platform broke.

Re-embedding pass: two-phase migration. Phase 1: write `embedding_v2` alongside `embedding` over time. Phase 2: at 95% coverage, switch read traffic + keep old column for 1 week rollback option. Cost: ~$20-50 for 10K profiles + 5K jobs at current pricing. Cheap relative to getting it wrong. Next maturity step: pre-deployment shadow comparison — run both versions in parallel for a week before flipping read traffic.

### White-label as a runtime config, not a build step — how one app becomes many

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/white-label-runtime-config-vs-build-step
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

GymApp's member app is one React Native binary shared by every gym. At launch, the app fetches the tenant's branding row (primary_color, logo_url, app_identifier) and the React tree reads from GymConfigContext. The app becomes that gym's app at runtime, not build time. One binary, N tenants, one App Store account.

Build-time white-labeling: new tenant = new build = new App Store submission = new review cycle. Multiply by N tenants and operational overhead scales linearly. Runtime: insert a row in gyms table. Done. Assets live on CDN; first launch caches locally; per-tenant weight typically <5MB. Multi-tenancy enforced by gymId foreign key on every domain model + middleware-scoped queries that filter automatically. Per-tenant features as feature flags on the gym row, never as per-tenant code branches.

Trade: structurally-different per-tenant apps still need per-tenant builds. For 80% of white-label cases where tenants want their colors + logo + features, runtime config is the right call.

### Socket.io + Redis pub/sub across PM2 cluster workers — live occupancy without polling

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/socketio-redis-pubsub-pm2-cluster
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Socket.io stores connection state in process memory by default. Across PM2 cluster (multiple Node processes) or multiple boxes behind a load balancer, emits from one worker can't reach connections on another — vanilla setup loses half the emits.

`@socket.io/redis-adapter` replaces in-memory bus with Redis pub/sub. Every emit publishes to Redis; every worker subscribes. Worker 1 receives turnstile webhook → emits `occupancy:updated` on `gym:${gymId}` room → Redis adapter publishes → all workers deliver to locally-connected clients. Client doesn't care which worker holds its WebSocket.

GymApp live-occupancy flow: NFC tap → scanner-bridge POSTs `/api/visits` → API authenticates + inserts visit + increments counter + emits to gym room → every staff dashboard + member home tab + lobby TV updates within ~50ms median. Rooms scoped to gymId — security boundary. Single Redis instance serves Socket.io adapter + rate-limit token bucket + cache + embedding-worker queue. Same pattern works for SSE if you only need server-to-client.

### node-hid as a hardware-abstraction layer — decoupling NFC scanners from the API

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/node-hid-nfc-scanner-bridge-pattern
Date: 2026-05-14. 6 min read.

GymApp's scanner-bridge is a small Node service on a Raspberry Pi at each gate. Uses `node-hid` to read card UIDs off USB NFC readers and POSTs `/api/visits` with the UID. Bridge knows hardware (USB device discovery, HID frame parsing, vendor protocols). API knows business logic (member lookup, visit insert, occupancy emit). Neither knows the other's details.

Auth via per-gym API key in the bridge's env file, sent in Authorization header. Key scoped to visits endpoint only — least-privilege. Bridge runs under systemd, auto-starts on boot. Updates push over SSH; the API never updates the Pi. Network outage handling: bridge queues visits to local SQLite, drains on reconnect, configurable max-age discards stale queued visits.

Pattern generalizes to payment terminal integrations, IoT sensors, thermal-printer receipts, scale integrations — anywhere hardware specifics shouldn't leak into the main API.

### Brand-as-filesystem-config — adding a tenant without a code change

URL: https://portfolio-seven-opal-35.vercel.app/notes/social-command-center-brand-as-filesystem-config
Date: 2026-05-14. 7 min read.

Social Command Center adds a brand by creating `brands/<slug>/` with `config.json` + `knowledge-base/` (markdown files describing products, voice, audience, recent campaigns). Commit + push. Next BullMQ cron run picks up the new directory. Six-stage pipeline walks each brand: Brand Discovery → Research → Strategy → Content Gen → Quality Gate → Post Creation.

Why filesystem not database: knowledge base is mostly long-form text. Markdown in git gets you version history, diff-on-PR review, branch-based experiments, grep across all brands, no admin UI to build. Trade: brands are a code-deploy concern (push to change). For operator-run platform with 7 brands, faster than any UI. For self-service hundreds of tenants, you'd want a database.

Quality gate: AI-checks-AI with explicit criteria from knowledge base ("is this on-brand? hook + payoff + CTA? avoid negative-pattern phrases?"). Posts that fail go back to Content Gen with feedback; two retries; mark `needs-review` after. State machine — discovery → research → strategy → content gen → quality gate → awaiting_image → scheduled → posted — every post at known state at all times. Postiz REST API handles platform-specific publishing.

Zero-API-cost path: Claude Code slash commands (`/analyze-brand`, `/generate-content-plan`, `/generate-content`) read the knowledge base directly from disk and POST `/api/import-content`. Operator can generate 12 weeks of content for all 7 brands without touching OpenAI bill.
